newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Golden Hope to phase out cocoa by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Golden Hope to phase out cocoa by 1999.

text.p: Malaysia's Golden Hope Plantations Bhd said on Wednesday it would convert all of its cocoa crop to oil palm by June 30, 1999.
The move reflected the poor performance of the group's cocoa sector, Golden Hope group chief executive Abdul Rahman Ramli told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
For the financial year ended June 30, 1996, the cocoa division incurred an operating loss of 1.07 million ringgit, against a 3.41 million ringgit loss the previous year.
Analysts had widely expected Golden Hope to phase out cocoa in favour of oil palm given the continuing depressed cocoa prices.
A total of 1,943 hectares of cocoa was converted to oil palm during the 1995/96 financial year, the company's annual report showed.
By the end of June this year, Golden Hope had about 80,000 hectares under oil palm, 28,000 hectares under rubber and 9,500 hectares under cocoa.

The group's cocoa area was boosted by the acquisition in April of BAL Plantations Malaysia Sdn Bhd, the country's oldest and largest cocoa grower, from London-based Commonwealth Development Corp for 380 million ringgit.

BAL, which covers 16,437 hectares of oil palm, cocoa and rubber grounds in eastern Sabah state, also runs two palm oil mills, three cocoa factories, a rubber factory and a bulking installation for palm oil.
